idiom_name: reserved sentinel message on a FIFO work queue
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: agree on one reserved message, value or tag that no work payload can equal (a dedicated type, tag field or enum), have each consumer loop with the queue's blocking take, and let it exit after it dequeues that value following its final work item. Production must stop before the pills are enqueued, and the injector must know the consumer count (one pill per consumer) so that no worker is left blocked. Where the runtime offers a completion primitive on the queue itself (channel close, CompleteAdding, Queue#close, finish), prefer it; the sentinel form is the portable fallback for queues without one.
code_sketch:
POISON = sentinel_value      # distinct from every work item

# producer, after the last real item:
for _ in range(consumers):
    queue.put(POISON)

# consumer:
while True:
    msg = queue.take()       # blocks while the queue is empty
    if msg is POISON:        # drain finished
        cleanup()
        break
    handle(msg)
pitfalls: One pill per consumer: a missing pill blocks a worker forever, an extra pill stops another worker early.
The sentinel must be collision-free with work payloads; use a tagged variant or type, not a magic value.
Enqueue pills only after production has stopped and after the last work item; ordering is the drain guarantee.
Without a join/ack and a deadline, shutdown cannot distinguish "all consumers exited" from "workers are still draining".

A worker blocked on queue.get() with no timeout never checks the sentinel; always use the queue's blocking take with a path to check shutdown state, or use queue.get(timeout=N) combined with a separate shutdown event.
Using None or 0 as a sentinel when the queue legitimately carries nullable/zero values silently corrupts the drain; use a tagged wrapper or type-discriminated union.

Memory visibility: on platforms with weak memory models (some JVM implementations, ARM cores), a pill write published to the queue before a concurrent work-item write may become visible to the consumer out of order; use a synchronisation primitive (mutex, happens-before rule, or a memory barrier) to guarantee the pill is visible only after all preceding items.

On weakly-ordered architectures (ARM, POWER), a consumer checking a volatile boolean flag before a blocking queue take must also synchronise after the take to re-read the flag; a stale flag value causes the consumer to exit before the pill arrives.

A consumer that has taken the pill but not yet exited holds the last reference to shared queue state; any cleanup that accesses that state (logging, metrics) is a use-after-free if it races with deallocation.

Wrong move: assume a bounded queue always has room for all shutdown pills -> the close coordinator can block while producers keep filling it, delaying or deadlocking shutdown -> instead quiesce producers first, coordinate capacity, or use the queue's completion API.

Wrong move: send Akka Classic PoisonPill to an Akka Typed actor -> Typed does not support PoisonPill's auto-received semantics -> instead define a typed Stop/Shutdown command that transitions to Behaviors.stopped.

https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/concurrent/BlockingQueue.html - JDK documents end-of-stream/poison objects as the shutdown tactic for blocking queues.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/collections/thread-safe/blockingcollection-overview - CompleteAdding/IsCompleted/GetConsumingEnumerable: the completion protocol that absorbs the sentinel.
https://kotlinlang.org/docs/channels.html - close described as sending a special close token that ends iteration after the buffered elements.
https://doc.akka.io/api/akka-core/current/akka/actor/PoisonPill.html - PoisonPill, a message all actors understand that terminates the actor when processed.
https://go.dev/blog/pipelines - Go blog on pipelines and cancellation, showing close(done) as a broadcast signal to unblock all senders in a concurrent pipeline.
https://go101.org/article/channel-closing.html - Go 101 on channel closing principles, including the moderator pattern for M-receiver/N-sender graceful shutdown.
https://pymotw.com/2/multiprocessing/communication.html - Python Module of the Week: JoinableQueue with None as sentinel for multiprocessing worker pools.
https://docs.python.org/3/library/multiprocessing.html - Python multiprocessing Queue documentation; sentinel values and JoinableQueue.join() for drain tracking.
https://igor.gorovyy.pro/blog/posts/2026-08-22-graceful-shutdown/ - Igor Gorovyy: graceful shutdown in Go with signal.NotifyContext, ordered component shutdown, and bounded deadline.
https://www.java-design-patterns.com/patterns/poison-pill/ - Java Design Patterns: poison pill with Producer/Consumer code examples and benefits/tradeoffs.

https://scalemind.dev/java/concurrency/poison-pill-shutdown-pattern-in-java/ - ScaleMind: Java poison pill decision guide, common mistakes (sending too few pills, enqueuing poison too early), and when it fits vs. when it becomes risky.
https://depot.dev/blog/graceful-shutdown-in-go - Depot: graceful shutdown in Go with context.Background() for detached operations during drain, and sync.WaitGroup for tracking in-flight work.
https://tokio.rs/tokio/topics/shutdown - Tokio: CancellationToken for cooperative shutdown across multiple tasks, with clone-based broadcasting.

https://async-concurrency.com/resilience-cancellation-error-handling/graceful-shutdown-and-signals/ - async-concurrency.com: phase-ordered shutdown (LB deregistration, drain, cancel, close), bounded deadlines, and signal handler placement on the event loop.

https://www.toolsku.com/en/blog/rust-tokio-graceful-shutdown-2026/ - ToolsKu: Tokio shutdown pitfalls including forgetting cancelled() in select, misusing CancellationToken as one-shot, and task leak detection.

https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-redis-poison-pill-pattern-queues/view - OneUpTime: dual Redis poison pill patterns - graceful shutdown via sentinel and dead-letter handling for poison/bad messages after retry exhaustion.

https://www.boundev.com/blog/dotnet-cancellationtoken-guide-async-patterns - Boundev: .NET CancellationToken patterns including linked tokens, Register() callbacks, and IHostApplicationLifetime integration.

https://serard.dev/content/blog/distributed-task/08-resilience.html - Stéphane Erard: saga DLH patterns, compensation failure handling, and circuit-breaker-wrapped retry policies for distributed task processing.

https://sph.sh/en/posts/dead-letter-queue-production-strategies/ - SPH: DLQ production strategies including exponential backoff with jitter, circuit-breaker DLQ routing, and content-based poison routing.

https://dev.to/rosgluk/dead-letter-queues-handling-poison-messages-in-distributed-systems-7p3 - DEV.to: distinguishing poison messages from transient failures, idempotency for DLQ redrive, and DLQ retention/alerting design.
https://codesprintpro.com/blog/microservices-patterns/ - Code Sprint Pro: Dead Letter Queue with retry/DLQ routing code examples, distinguishing recoverable vs. permanent errors, and DLQ monitoring.

https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_85_0/doc/html/boost_asio/example/cpp14/executors/pipeline.cpp - Boost ASIO pipeline example: queue_front::stop() sets a flag and notify_all to unblock all consumers cooperatively.

https://floriancourouge.com/en/blog/kafka-poison-pills-patterns-resilience-consumers - Florian Courouge: Kafka poison pill resilience - DLQ, Skip & Log, Retry with exponential backoff and circuit breaker, Quarantine Topic pattern, and observability setup with Prometheus/Grafana.

https://www.conduktor.io/blog/dead-letter-topics-handling-poison-pills - Conduktor: dead letter topic handling for Kafka poison pills, ErrorHandlingDeserializer, Spring Kafka @RetryableTopic with @DltHandler, and replay strategy.

https://www.confluent.io/blog/spring-kafka-can-your-kafka-consumers-handle-a-poison-pill/ - Confluent/ING: Spring Kafka poison pill at ING - deserialisation failures blocking partitions, ErrorHandlingDeserializer configuration, and DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer.

https://github.com/akka/akka/blob/main/akka-actor/src/main/scala/akka/actor/Actor.scala - Akka source: PoisonPill case object extends AutoReceivedMessage with PossiblyHarmful; lifecycle hooks preStart, postStop, preRestart, postRestart; actor mailbox continues processing ahead of the pill.

https://github.com/akka/akka-core/blob/v2.10.21/akka-actor/src/main/scala/akka/pattern/GracefulStopSupport.scala - Akka GracefulStopSupport: gracefulStop(target, timeout, stopMessage=PoisonPill) returns a Future[Boolean] that completes when the actor has processed all existing messages and terminated.

https://www.erlang.org/docs/25/reference_manual/processes.html - Erlang OTP official documentation: bidirectional link/exit signals, exit(Pid, Reason) for explicit termination, monitor/2 for unidirectional observation, and trap_exit for converting signals to messages; Erlang uses exit signals as a more powerful built-in alternative to a sentinel pill.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/competing-consumers - Microsoft Azure Architecture Patterns: Competing Consumers - multiple consumers on a queue, poison message detection via dead-letter queues after MaxDeliveryCount, and transactional read operations.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/queue-based-load-leveling - Microsoft Azure Architecture Patterns: Queue-Based Load Leveling - buffer between task and service; Service Bus dead-letter sub-queue for messages that exceed delivery attempts.

https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/java/util/concurrent/BlockingQueue.html - JDK 26 documents that BlockingQueue has no built-in shutdown and that producers commonly use a sentinel/end-of-stream object.
https://docs.python.org/3/library/multiprocessing.html - Python multiprocessing docs cover FIFO queues, sentinel-based worker termination, and joining workers after shutdown.

https://doc.akka.io/libraries/akka-core/current/actors.html - Akka Classic docs: PoisonPill is enqueued like ordinary messages and processed after already-queued messages; Kill is the forceful alternative.
https://doc.akka.io/libraries/akka-core/current/typed/from-classic.html - Akka docs: PoisonPill is not supported in Akka Typed; use a protocol-specific stop message instead.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.concurrent.blockingcollection-1.completeadding?view=net-10.0 - BlockingCollection.CompleteAdding prevents new additions and lets consuming loops finish without sentinels.
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/8667870/is-it-possible-to-use-poison-pill-approach-with-bounded-queues - discussion of bounded-queue shutdown caveats when a full queue cannot accept poison pills.
